union.summary: Insert/delete row-column, copy/paste and cut-redirect throw "Invalid Reference" on any formula containing an unbounded range
union.evidence: The new grammar makes `A:A` / `1:1` / `A1:B` lex as a single `REFERENCE` token, and every formula-rewriting helper splits a range token on ':' and calls `parseARef` on each half: shifting.ts:373-374 (`shiftFormula`), shifting.ts:80-81 (`moveFormula`), shifting.ts:184-185 (`relocateFormula`), shifting.ts:242-243 (`redirectFormula`). `parseARef` matches `/^(\$?)([A-Za-z]+)(\$?)(\d+)$/` (coordinates.ts:366) and throws for the endpoint `A` (no digits) or `1` (no letters). None of these are wrapped in try/catch: `MemStore.shiftCells` -> `shiftGrid` -> `shiftFormula` (memory.ts:181, shifting.ts:456), `moveGrid` (shifting.ts:120), paste `relocateGrid` (clipboard.ts:25 and :151), cut redirect `redirectFormulasForCut` (sheet.ts:2375). So on a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)`, inserting/deleting a row or column, copying the cell, or cut-pasting anything raises an unhandled exception, aborting the operation mid-way (dimension maps/styles are shifted around the throw).

union.summary: Cross-sheet unbounded refs (`Sheet2!A:A`) reach `toSrefs` unexpanded and throw instead of evaluating to #ERROR!
union.evidence: `expandUnboundedRanges` deliberately skips cross-sheet refs (formula.ts:364), but `Sheet2!A:A` still lexes as one REFERENCE (grammar: `SHEET_NAME '!' REFRANGE`, and REFRANGE now accepts `COL:COL`). `toSrefs` handles the cross-sheet case first and calls `parseRange(localRef)` -> `parseRef('A')`, which throws at coordinates.ts:336-338. The `isCrossSheetRef(r) continue` guards are *inside* the for-of body, so the generator throws before the guard runs: memory.ts:333-334, yorkie-store.ts:574-577 / 585-588 / 601-604. `Sheet.fetchGridByReferences` (sheet.ts:2615) has the same problem for the expanded formula produced in calculator.ts:94-95. Result: typing `=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)` throws out of `setData`/`buildDependantsMap` (no catch in sheet.ts:1063-1073), instead of the documented `#ERROR!` (docs/design/sheets/formula.md claims it evaluates to `#ERROR!`).

union.summary: `buildGlobalDependantsMap` still uses the raw formula, so a local unbounded ref in any cross-sheet-touching formula crashes cross-sheet recalculation
union.evidence: sheet.ts:2711-2712 (`extractReferences(cell.f)` then `toSrefs(references)`) and sheet.ts:2736-2738 (same for every formula of every remote sheet) were not given the `expandUnboundedRanges` treatment that MemStore/YorkieStore `buildDependantsMap` got. A formula such as `=SUM(A:A)+Sheet2!B1` yields the reference `A:A`, and `toSrefs` -> `parseRange('A:A')` -> `parseRef('A')` throws (coordinates.ts:336). This runs inside `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2799) with only a `finally`, so the exception escapes and cross-sheet refresh dies for the whole workbook.

union.summary: Clearing the last populated cell of a referenced column/row leaves the dependent formula permanently stale (wrong value persisted)
union.evidence: The dependants map is built from the *post-edit* bounds: `removeData` deletes the cells first (sheet.ts:1128-1131) and only then calls `buildDependantsMap` (sheet.ts:1144), which expands `A:A` with `this.cellIndex.bounds()` taken after the delete (memory.ts:325-333). Scenario: A1=10,A2=20,A3=30, D1=`=SUM(A:A)` shows 60; clear A3 -> bounds shrink to maxR=2 -> `A:A` expands to `A1:A2` -> the map has no `A3` key -> `topologicalSort(map, {A3})` yields only A3 -> D1 is never recalculated and keeps the persisted value 60 while the column sums 30. It stays wrong until some cell still inside the shrunken range changes. The design note only reasons about the growth direction ("cells added beyond the prior extent are picked up on their own write"); the shrink direction is unguarded, and the new tests only cover growth (calculation.test.ts:348-356).

union.summary: Blank-cell skip in `Arguments.iterate` silently changes results for ordinary bounded ranges across ~18 functions
union.evidence: arguments.ts:116-123 now skips any cell in a *range* whose `v` is undefined/''. `iterate` is shared by SUM, PRODUCT, GCD, LCM, SUMSQ, AVERAGE, MEDIAN, MIN, MAX, STDEV/STDEVP, VAR/VARP, MODE, GEOMEAN, HARMEAN, AVEDEV, DEVSQ and AND/OR/XOR. Previously `ref2num`/`ref2bool` coerced a missing cell to 0/false and it was counted. So bounded ranges change behavior too: `=AVERAGE(A1:A3)` with A2 blank now divides by 2 instead of 3; `=PRODUCT(A1:A3)` with a blank no longer returns 0; `=AND(A1:A3)` on an all-blank range now returns TRUE (vacuous) where it previously returned FALSE (Excel returns #VALUE!); `=AVERAGE(A:A)` over an empty column hits `count === 0` and returns #VALUE! (functions-statistical.ts:39-41) where Sheets returns #DIV/0!. Several of these move toward Excel semantics, but the change is not scoped to unbounded ranges and is not covered by tests, so existing bounded-range results shift unannounced.

union.summary: `getUsedBounds` is re-read per cell inside the `calculate` loop, so one recalculation pass can use inconsistent extents
union.evidence: calculator.ts:90-93 awaits `sheet.getUsedBounds()` for every formula cell, while the loop itself writes cells (anchor value at :136 and spill ghosts at :141). A spill (or a formula result) written early in the pass can extend the used extent, so a later `=SUM(A:A)` in the same pass expands over a larger range than an earlier identical formula — results become dependent on topological order. Worse, the dependants map used for that pass was built with the pre-pass bounds, so cells added during the pass are not registered as dependencies and will not trigger later recalcs.

union.summary: `resolveRange` expands against the whole-sheet bounding box, not the referenced column/row, producing huge ranges and dependants maps
union.evidence: coordinates.ts:458-467 fills an omitted row with `bounds[1].r` and an omitted column with `bounds[1].c`, where `CellIndex.bounds()` (cell-index.ts:128-149) is the global min/max over *all* populated cells. With one cell at Z100000, `=SUM(A:A)` expands to `A1:A100000`, and `fetchGridByReferences` then performs one awaited `store.get` per cell (sheet.ts:2615-2629) while `buildDependantsMap` inserts 100000 Map/Set entries per such formula (memory.ts:333). Explicit endpoints are also not clamped, so `=SUM(2:5)` on 3 rows of data materializes rows 4-5 across all columns. Correctness-wise the values are right, but the unbounded allocation per keystroke is a real freeze/OOM risk.

union.summary: YorkieStore bounds can silently drop pending batch writes when the index is marked dirty mid-batch
union.evidence: `getUsedBounds`/`buildDependantsMap` call `ensureIndex()` (yorkie-store.ts:615-616, 564), which rebuilds the index solely from the Yorkie document (yorkie-store.ts:194-204). Overlay writes only update the index when `!this.dirty` (yorkie-store.ts:266-273, 331-333). If a remote change sets `dirty` during a batch (paste/sort), the rebuild discards the overlay-added cells, so `bounds()` under-reports the extent and unbounded refs expand too small — producing a silently low SUM/COUNT for that batch.

union.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` swallows all resolve failures, degrading to an evaluation error with no signal
union.evidence: formula.ts:379-385: `try { ... } catch { /* Fall through to the original text */ }`. Any future mismatch between what the lexer accepts as an unbounded REFRANGE and what `parsePartialRef` accepts silently leaves the raw text in place, which then surfaces as a generic `#ERROR!` from `evaluate` (formula.ts:614-616) with no way to tell expansion failed.

union.summary: Inserting/deleting a row or column, autofill/copy, or cut-paste throws `Invalid Reference` when any formula contains an unbounded range (`=SUM(A:A)`)
union.evidence: `shiftFormula` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:370-374) takes the `text.includes(':')` branch for the newly-lexable `A:A` token and calls `parseARef(startStr)`; `parseARef` (coordinates.ts:366) matches `^(\$?)([A-Za-z]+)(\$?)(\d+)$` and throws `Invalid Reference` for the endpoint `A`. `shiftFormula` is reached from `shiftGrid` (shifting.ts:456) ← `MemStore.shiftCells` (memory.ts:181) ← `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1218), which has no try/catch, so `insertRows`/`deleteColumns` reject. The same unguarded `parseARef(startStr)` exists in `relocateFormula` (shifting.ts:184-185, reached from `cloneCellForAutofill`, clipboard.ts:151) and `redirectFormula` (shifting.ts:242-243, reached from `redirectFormulasForCut`, sheet.ts:2375). The new grammar/expansion added no guard on any of these call sites.

union.summary: A cross-sheet unbounded ref (`=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)`) throws instead of evaluating to `#ERROR!`, breaking every subsequent edit on the sheet
union.evidence: `expandUnboundedRanges` deliberately skips cross-sheet refs (formula.ts:362-365), so `SHEET2!A:A` survives into `extractReferences`. In `MemStore.buildDependantsMap` (memory.ts:333) the `isCrossSheetRef(r) continue` guard is *inside* the loop body, but the generator `toSrefs` (coordinates.ts:236-243) already calls `parseRange('A:A')` → `parseRef('A')` → `throw new Error('Invalid Reference')` while producing the item. `buildDependantsMap` iterates the whole grid on every edit (sheet.ts:1063), so one such formula makes all later `setData` calls reject. The same pattern exists in yorkie-store.ts:574-576, 585-587, 601-603, and in calculator.ts:94-95 → `Sheet.fetchGridByReferences` (sheet.ts:2615), which also calls `toSrefs` before its `isCrossSheetRef` check and is not wrapped in try/catch. docs/design/sheets/formula.md claims these "evaluate to `#ERROR!`" — they actually throw.

union.summary: `buildGlobalDependantsMap` passes unexpanded formulas to `toSrefs`, so a local `A:A` inside any cross-sheet formula throws during cross-sheet recalculation
union.evidence: sheet.ts:2711-2712 (`extractReferences(cell.f)` → `toSrefs(references)`) and sheet.ts:2736-2738 were not given the `expandUnboundedRanges` treatment that MemStore/YorkieStore got. For a formula such as `=SUM(A:A)+Sheet2!B1` the local token `A:A` reaches `toSrefs` → `parseRange('A:A')` → `parseRef('A')` → throws. `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2796-2804) has only a `finally`, so the rejection propagates to the caller.

union.summary: `resolveRange` normalizes with `toRange`, so an open-ended range anchored past the data extent expands backwards and includes cells outside the reference
union.evidence: coordinates.ts:458-467: `toRange({r: a.r ?? 1, ...}, {r: b.r ?? max.r, ...})` and `toRange` (coordinates.ts:97-108) takes min/max of the two endpoints. With bounds maxR=3, `A5:A` yields from={5,1}, to={3,1} → normalized to `A3:A5`, so `=SUM(A5:A)` wrongly includes A3 (and A4). Likewise `=AVERAGE(B2:B)` when only row 1 is populated becomes `B1:B2` and averages B1. The same happens column-wise: `D1:1` with maxC=2 becomes `B1:D1`. The correct result is an empty/collapsed range at the explicit anchor.

union.summary: Deleting the cell that defined the used extent leaves whole-column/row formulas stale (no dependants-map entry for the removed cell)
union.evidence: `buildDependantsMap` expands `A:A` against the *post-mutation* bounds (memory.ts:325,333; called at sheet.ts:1063 and sheet.ts:1144 after the store write/delete). Sequence: A1..A3 populated, D1=`=SUM(A:A)` → 60; set A10=5 → bounds maxR=10 → 65; now clear A10 → the delete happens first (sheet.ts:1055/1130), bounds shrink back to maxR=3, so the rebuilt map contains keys A1..A3 only. `changedSrefs={A10}` has no dependants, `topologicalSort` yields just A10 (no formula), so D1 keeps displaying 65 instead of 60. Only the growth direction is covered by the new test (calculation.test.ts 'picks up a newly added cell beyond the prior data extent').

union.summary: Skipping blank cells inside ranges changes results of pre-existing bounded-range formulas; `AND` over an all-blank range flips from FALSE to TRUE
union.evidence: arguments.ts:110-125 now `continue`s for any range cell with `!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === ''`. `andFunc` (functions-logical.ts:111-121) iterates `BoolArgs.iterate` and returns `{bool,true}` when nothing is yielded, so `=AND(A1:A3)` over blanks now returns TRUE (previously `ref2bool('')` → false → FALSE; Excel returns #VALUE!). Same class of silent change for `AVERAGE` denominators, `STDEV/VAR` (`values.length < 2` → now #VALUE! where it previously had values), `XOR`, and `GCD/LCM` on existing bounded ranges — the guard has no opt-out for callers that relied on blanks-as-zero. Also note a cell with `f` set but `v` not yet computed is treated as blank.

union.summary: Blanks are skipped but text cells are still coerced to 0, so `MIN`/`AVERAGE` over a whole column with a text header returns a wrong number
union.evidence: arguments.ts:116-123 only skips empty cells; non-numeric strings still flow through `ref2num` (arguments.ts:157-165) which returns `numNode(0)` for `Number('foo')` → NaN. The new test at test/formula/formula.test.ts:4423-4429 codifies `=MIN(A1:A2)` over `'foo','bar'` → `0`. Consequently `=MIN(A:A)` on a column with a text header returns 0, and `=AVERAGE(A:A)` divides by the header row (`'Name',10,20` → 10 instead of 15). Excel/Sheets ignore text in ranges; with whole-column refs headers are the common case.

union.summary: Bounds are re-read per cell inside the calculation loop, so expansions are order-dependent within a single recalculation pass
union.evidence: calculator.ts:90-93 calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` for every formula cell inside the `for (const sref of sorted)` loop, while the loop itself writes cells (`sheet.setCell`, spill ghosts at calculator.ts:136-141). A formula evaluated early in the pass therefore clamps `A:A` to a smaller extent than one evaluated after a spill/write extended the extent, making results depend on topological order rather than on sheet content.

union.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` swallows resolve failures and returns the unexpanded text, which then crashes downstream instead of yielding an error value
union.evidence: formula.ts:379-385 catches any exception from `resolveRange`/`toSrng` and falls through to `body += token.text`. The unexpanded token then reaches `extractReferences` → `toSrefs` in `fetchGridByReferences` (sheet.ts:2615) / `buildDependantsMap`, where `parseRange` throws an uncaught error. A local failure should be turned into an error value (or the ref dropped), not deferred to a code path with no handler.

Same class of silent change for `AVERAGE` denominators, `STDEV/VAR` (`values.length < 2` → now #VALUE! where it previously had values), `XOR`, and `GCD/LCM` on existing bounded ranges — the guard has no opt-out for callers that relied on blanks-as-zero. Also note a cell with `f` set but `v` not yet computed is treated as blank.

per_sample.summary: Blanks are skipped but text cells are still coerced to 0, so `MIN`/`AVERAGE` over a whole column with a text header returns a wrong number
per_sample.evidence: arguments.ts:116-123 only skips empty cells; non-numeric strings still flow through `ref2num` (arguments.ts:157-165) which returns `numNode(0)` for `Number('foo')` → NaN. The new test at test/formula/formula.test.ts:4423-4429 codifies `=MIN(A1:A2)` over `'foo','bar'` → `0`. Consequently `=MIN(A:A)` on a column with a text header returns 0, and `=AVERAGE(A:A)` divides by the header row (`'Name',10,20` → 10 instead of 15). Excel/Sheets ignore text in ranges; with whole-column refs headers are the common case.

per_sample.summary: Bounds are re-read per cell inside the calculation loop, so expansions are order-dependent within a single recalculation pass
per_sample.evidence: calculator.ts:90-93 calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` for every formula cell inside the `for (const sref of sorted)` loop, while the loop itself writes cells (`sheet.setCell`, spill ghosts at calculator.ts:136-141). A formula evaluated early in the pass therefore clamps `A:A` to a smaller extent than one evaluated after a spill/write extended the extent, making results depend on topological order rather than on sheet content.

per_sample.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` swallows resolve failures and returns the unexpanded text, which then crashes downstream instead of yielding an error value
per_sample.evidence: formula.ts:379-385 catches any exception from `resolveRange`/`toSrng` and falls through to `body += token.text`. The unexpanded token then reaches `extractReferences` → `toSrefs` in `fetchGridByReferences` (sheet.ts:2615) / `buildDependantsMap`, where `parseRange` throws an uncaught error. A local failure should be turned into an error value (or the ref dropped), not deferred to a code path with no handler.
